SceneEditor.Title: Scene Director
SceneEditor.AddCharacterControlHint: Re-adjusts an already on-stage character — appearance, movement, obscure/reveal, and position — without ever giving them a fresh entrance. Does nothing if this character isn't currently staged.
SceneEditor.StageCharacterHint: Pick any number of characters from an image grid (checking one adds an amber glow), then firing this section stages every checked one at once — a multi-select alternative to Add Character for bringing a whole group on stage in one step. A Group token on the board expands into its own header with its members listed underneath, no token needed for the members themselves. Once staged, use Character Control to move/effect any of them individually.
SceneEditor.StageCharacterAlwaysActiveHint: This card has no timer — it doesn't wait on anything. During Auto Play it fires and moves straight to the next section instead of pausing first.
SceneEditor.ClearSceneHint: Resets what's currently staged/captioned right now, for you and everyone else. Does not delete anything in this scene's timeline.
SceneEditor.AddClearSceneHint: Inserts an End Scene step into the timeline. When Next (or its own Fire button) reaches this step, it wipes every staged character/caption/background effect for you and everyone else, exactly like the manual Clear Scene button below — just scripted into the scene itself, so a scene can reset cleanly on its own without you reaching for that button by hand.
SceneEditor.AutoPlayHint: Runs through this scene's timeline on its own, one section at a time, pacing itself by each section's own delay (the clock icon's number box). Stops automatically at the end, or at a Scene Controls (pause) section until you click Continue.
SceneEditor.AutoPausedBanner: Auto Play paused — click Continue when ready.
SceneEditor.AddSceneControlsHint: Inserts a Pause step into the timeline. Auto Play stops here and waits for you to click Continue instead of auto-advancing on a timer — place it right after whichever section you want Auto Play to stop after. Manually stepping past it (Next, or its own Fire button) does nothing; it only matters to Auto Play.
SceneEditor.ScenePauseFireHint: This section only does something during Auto Play (it pauses there). Manually firing or stepping past it does nothing.
SceneEditor.SkipInAutoPlayHint: When on (yellow), Auto Play skips straight past this Pause without stopping — lets you bypass a checkpoint temporarily without deleting it. Off by default: every Pause stops Auto Play until you click Continue. Never affects manual Next/Fire, which already skip every Pause either way.
SceneEditor.AutoDelayHint: How long this section's own Auto Play delay is (ms) — whether that's the wait AFTER it fires (before the next section) or BEFORE it fires depends on the "Auto Play timing" setting in Config Settings. Only used during Auto Play — manual Next/Fire ignore it.
SceneEditor.ExpandGroupHint: This character is a Group actor. Adds one Character section per party member for the members that already have a token on this scene, instead of staging the whole group as one portrait.
SceneEditor.ImageSourceLooseHint: This character has no token on this scene (picked from a Group's member list), so it can only be staged with its actor's own profile art.
SceneEditor.LockSceneHint: Locks this scene so it can be fired from ANY Foundry scene, as long as each character has a token placed wherever you currently are. Converts every character reference here from a specific placed token to the character itself, then freezes editing — Add/Delete/Clear, field changes, reordering, renaming, and Position Locks all stop working until you Unlock. Fire Now, Next, and Auto Play keep working the whole time. Every character this scene uses needs a real token on the board you're currently viewing before this will work — it can't convert a reference it can't find right now.
SceneEditor.UnlockSceneHint: Unlocks this scene so you can edit it again — Fire Now/Next/Auto Play were never affected by the lock.
SceneEditor.SceneLockedBanner: This scene is locked. Fire Now / Next / Auto Play still work everywhere — click Unlock to edit it again.
SceneEditor.SceneLockedNotice: This scene is locked. Unlock it first.
SceneEditor.SceneLockFailedNotice: Couldn't lock this scene: {count} character reference(s) don't resolve on the Foundry scene you're currently viewing. Switch to the board where all of this scene's characters are placed, then try again.
SceneEditor.ShowAllCharacters: Show all characters in this scene
SceneEditor.NoActiveCharacters: (no characters currently on stage to clear)
SceneEditor.VisibilityHint: Public: posts to chat and lets FGA Character Popup (if installed) show its own popup instead — no Scene Director caption. Private: no chat post, shows Scene Director's own caption.
SceneEditor.BubbleHint: Private lines only. Shows this line in the fixed speech bubble (see Config Settings) instead of the caption bar — the bubble's tail points toward whichever side of the screen the speaking character is staged on.
SceneEditor.ImageSourceHint: Which art this staged portrait shows. Profile art is the actor's own portrait image (the default, same as before). Token art is the image shown on the map token itself, when it's different from the portrait — some art sets keep those separate.
SceneEditor.ObscureDurationHint: How long an Obscure style change animates when it fires on a character already on stage (e.g. switching from Blur to None to reveal them), instead of snapping instantly. Only matters when this section actually changes the obscure look — a section that leaves style/blur alone doesn't touch it. Instant on a character's first appearance for every style EXCEPT Fade In/Teleport In — those are entrance effects, so a brand-new character actually plays that reveal now instead of just popping in already visible. This is what used to be the separate "Reveal Character" section — that's now just part of Character Control.
SceneEditor.PositionLockHint: Gray = empty, click to save your character's current position there. Orange = has a saved position, click to jump back to it. Either way the slot turns red — that's THIS section's current slot; click it again to un-mark it without moving or losing the saved position. Shared by this character across every one of their Character/Character Control sections in this scene.
SceneEditor.PositionLockClearHint: Deletes the saved position from this character's currently active (red) lock slot. Disabled when no lock is active.
SceneEditor.TransitionEnabledHint: When this character is already staged and moves to a new position (e.g. firing this section again after a Position Lock recall), animate smoothly to the new spot instead of snapping there instantly. Off by default. Manual dragging is always an instant snap regardless of this.
SceneEditor.TransitionMsHint: Slide: how long the slide itself takes. Fade Movement/Teleport Movement: how long EACH half takes — the character fades/teleports away at its old spot over this many ms, snaps to the new spot while hidden, then fades/teleports back in there over the same amount again, so the whole move takes twice this.

Config.Title: Configure Scene Director
Config.OnScreenHint: Puts a live caption up on the actual game screen (only you can see it) so you can compare it to the little preview above while you adjust settings.
Config.OnScreenPreviewLine: This is what your caption looks like on the actual screen.
Config.BubbleOnScreenHint: Puts a real speech bubble up on the actual game screen (only you can see it) so you can check its size before using it live.

HideFloatingButton.Name: Hide floating button
HideFloatingButton.Hint: Hides the draggable floating icon. You can still open Scene Director from its button on the left-side toolbar.

EditorToolsDefaultVisible.Name: Editor tools default visibility
EditorToolsDefaultVisible.Hint: Whether the flip/rotate editing tools default to shown or hidden on the staging screen.

KeyboardNudgeEnabled.Name: Enable keyboard nudge
KeyboardNudgeEnabled.Hint: Lets arrow keys nudge a selected staged character's position without moving tokens on the map.

DefaultLineVisibility.Name: Default line visibility
DefaultLineVisibility.Hint: Whether new dialogue lines default to Public (posted to chat) or Private/bypass.

TransitionEnabled.Name: Default: slide to new position
TransitionEnabled.Hint: Each Character section has its own "Slide to new position" toggle (Movement subsection) — this is only the starting value newly-added Character sections are seeded with, and changing it doesn't affect any section that already exists. Off by default.

TransitionType.Name: Default: movement type
TransitionType.Hint: The starting movement style newly-added Character sections are seeded with (see the setting above) — each section's own Movement subsection can change it afterward.

AutoDelayOrder.Name: Auto Play timing
AutoDelayOrder.Hint: Does each section's own delay box (the clock icon in its row) count as the wait AFTER it fires, before Auto Play moves on to the next section — or the wait BEFORE it fires? Applies to every section's delay the same way. Only affects Auto Play — manual Next/Fire always ignore the delay box either way.
AutoDelayOrder.ActionThenTimer: Action, then Timer (fire now, wait before the next one)

DefaultImageSource.SectionTitle: Default image source by token type
DefaultImageSource.Hint: Which art (Profile or Token) a brand-new appearance of a character starts on, picked by what kind of token it is. Only applies the first time a subject is ever staged in a scene — picking the same character again, or re-firing Stage Character on someone already on stage, always keeps whatever image source they already had. A player-owned or "character"-type actor always uses the Player setting, even if its token's disposition happens to be Friendly.
